subject.title: [Bug]: Preflight compaction failure permanently locks Composer into "terminated" state

question: Should the canonical fix for this issue be the structured runtime retryability contract, UI/lifecycle recovery, or both?
rationale: The bug is real, but maintainer feedback already showed that a broad fail-open provider bucket can hide auth/request-shape errors, and multiple open PRs now compete on the exact boundary.

options.title: Runtime retryability contract
options.body: Treat timeout, explicit 429, and 5xx as skip/continue outcomes while preserving 400/401/403 and broad summary failures as terminal, with positive and negative tests plus proof.

options.title: UI recovery only
options.body: Keep compaction failure policy unchanged and make `chat.dispatch-error` recoverable in the Control UI, which avoids provider policy changes but may leave transient compaction failures as hard pre-run errors.

options.title: Runtime contract plus UI safety net
options.body: Land the narrow runtime fix first and add UI recovery only if after-fix proof still shows the Composer can wedge.

recommendation.title: Runtime retryability contract
recommendation.body: Treat timeout, explicit 429, and 5xx as skip/continue outcomes while preserving 400/401/403 and broad summary failures as terminal, with positive and negative tests plus proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They gave the prior maintainer feedback defining the safe retryability boundary and are already being asked for direction in the issue discussion.
